reference_circuits.name: VBAT/GPS_VBAT input reference circuit (Figure 5)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: The text recommends a 100uF low-ESR tantalum capacitor, a 1uF~10uF ceramic capacitor, 33pF and 10pF capacitors, and a 5.1V/500mW Zener diode placed as close as possible to VBAT pins; Figure 5 is named as the input reference circuit.

reference_circuits.name: LDO power supply reference circuit (Figure 6)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: A reference design for +5V input whose output power supply is 4.1V; a linear regulator can be used.

reference_circuits.name: DC-DC power supply reference circuit (Figure 7)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: A DC-DC reference circuit; the text calls it preferable for high input/output drop-out because of better efficiency, particularly with the module’s 2A burst peak.

reference_circuits.name: PWRKEY transistor and button circuits (Figures 10 and 11)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: Two powered-on/down circuits, one using a transistor and one a button; PWRKEY is internally pulled up to 3V and must be pulled low at least 1 second then released.

reference_circuits.name: GNSS RTC backup circuits (Figures 15–17)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: Reference circuits for RTC supply from an external capacitor, a non-chargeable battery, and a rechargeable battery through VRTC.

reference_circuits.name: UART level/interface circuits (Figures 19–22)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: Resistor matching and diode-isolation circuits for 3.0V/3.3V UART, plus TX and RX level-matching circuits for 5V UART.

reference_circuits.name: USB reference circuit (Figure 23)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: A USB reference circuit; the USB data-line TVS should be less than 5pF and traces should use differential form.

reference_circuits.name: Speaker and microphone reference circuits (Figures 28 and 29)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: Speaker and electret-microphone circuits with 10pF/33pF components and ESD markings; the text says audio signals should follow differential-signal layout rules.

reference_circuits.name: SIM-card-holder circuits (Figures 30 and 31)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: Reference circuits for 8-pin and 6-pin SIM card holders, showing 51Ω series components, 22pF capacitors, a 100nF capacitor, and ESDA6V1 text.

reference_circuits.name: SD reference circuit (Figure 34)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: An SD reference circuit; use VDD_EXT for a 2.8V SD-card supply or external LDO for 3.3V.

reference_circuits.name: NETLIGHT reference circuit (Figure 35)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: A NETLIGHT LED indication reference circuit with text labels VBAT, 4.7K and 47K.

reference_circuits.name: GSM antenna matching circuits (Figures 37 and 38)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: A matching circuit with RF connector and a version without it; R101/C101/C102 are matching components, normally R101 is 0Ω and C101/C102 are not mounted.

reference_circuits.name: GNSS passive and active antenna matching circuits (Figures 39 and 40)
reference_circuits.what_the_PDF_actually_shows: Passive and active GNSS antenna matching circuits; R101/C101/C102 values are determined after tuning, normally R101 is 0Ω and C101/C102 are not mounted.

pcb_considerations.assertion: Input voltage must never drop below 3.0V at 2A transmit burst; VBAT traces must be at least 60mil, and the power IC/bypass capacitor should be as close as possible to the module.
Keep antenna trace between pin output and connector as short as possible; do not route RF signal across the board; keep RF away from SIM card and power ICs.

Keep positive VBAT short and wide; route source to VBAT through Zener diode then large capacitor; make pins 36/37 shortest to source ground; do not trace signals over the upper layer of GND pads if possible.
Keep SIM holder away from antenna/RF cable and near the module; add ESD protection for SIM_CLK, SIM_DATA, SIM_RST, and SIM_VDD; keep those signals away from power/high-speed-frequency signals.
Keep SIM traces short and away from RF lines, VBAT, and high-speed signals; connect SIM-holder ground directly to main ground; shield the SIM signal with ground.
Keep audio traces away from antenna and power and avoid running audio in parallel with VBAT.
Route UART signals and USB signals in bundles.
Place audio filtering bypass capacitors near the module and another group near the connector; keep audio lines far from RF cable, antenna, and VBAT pin.

antenna_requirements.assertion: There are three antenna interfaces: GSM_ANT, GPS_ANT, BT_ANT.
Antenna input impedance should be 50Ω and VSWR less than 2; place GSM and BT antennas as far apart as possible and provide isolation greater than 30dB.
GSM_ANT connects an external GSM antenna. The connection must be DC-decoupled; an external antenna must be matched properly and a matching circuit is necessary.
GNSS interface connects the customer-board antenna; passive and active antennas are stated as normal options, and the external antenna must be matched properly.
For active GNSS antenna, VCC_ANT is needed on the customer application board; L101 should be no less than 27nH, and R102 protects the circuit if active antenna is shorted to ground.

protection_circuits.assertion: For VBAT/GPS_VBAT, the PDF strongly recommends a 5.1V/500mW Zener diode to prevent damage by voltage surge and gives a recommended-diode table.
SIM interface signals should be protected against ESD with a TVS diode array; the PDF recommends ST ESDA6V1-5W6 or ON SEMI SMF05C.
SIM design guidance: TVS parasitic capacitance should not exceed 50pF; 51Ω resistors on SIM_RST/SIM_CLK/SIM_DATA enhance ESD protection.
USB data-line TVS should be less than 5pF.

The GSM antenna connector is DC coupled to ground via an inductor for ESD protection; Table 31 lists Marata LXES03AAA1-154 (0201) and LXES15AAA1-153 (0402) as recommended transient-voltage suppressors.
The speaker/microphone reference circuits show ESD markings and 10pF/33pF components.

functional.test: Power-on readiness at fixed baud rate
functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for at least 1 second and release. To use the stated indication, configure and save a fixed baud rate with AT+IPR=x.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: At fixed baud rate, code “RDY” should be received from the serial port every time SIM868 is powered on; RDY does not appear when autobauding is active.

functional.method/procedure: Pull PWRKEY low for at least 1 second and release; the diagram gives 1s<T1<33s.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: Before completion the module sends “NORMAL POWER OFF”; STATUS is low when power-off mode is indicated.
Before completion the module sends “NORMAL POWER OFF”; STATUS is low when power-off mode is indicated.

functional.method/procedure: With autobauding enabled, send “AT”, “at”, “aT”, or “At” until the DTE receives a response. The DTE must be set to 8 data bits, no parity, and 1 stop bit.
functional.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: Receipt of “OK” means DTE and DCE are correctly synchronized.
The 1PPS signal will come out after successfully positioning.

communication.method/procedure: Power on SIM868, then connect USB_VBUS, USB_DP, USB_DM, and GND to a PC.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: When SIM868 detects USB_VBUS and can communicate normally with USB_DP/USB_DM, it enters USB download mode automatically.

communication.method/procedure: The document states that conducted receiving sensitivity is tested under static condition.
Tables 40 and 41 report conducted output power and state conformance to 3GPP TS 05.05.
communication.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: At maximum power, GSM900/GSM850 output should not exceed 33dBm (tolerance ±2dB normal, ±2.5dB extreme); DCS1800/PCS1900 should not exceed 30dBm with the same stated maximum-level tolerances.

power.method/procedure: Figure 8 states VBAT=4.0V, CA=100µF tantalum (ESR=0.7Ω), CB=1uF~10uF, and a 2A burst.
power.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: Figure 8 labels the maximum VBAT drop as 350mV.
≤3.5V reports UNDER-VOLTAGE WARNNING; ≥4.3V reports OVER-VOLTAGE WARNNING; <3.4V reports UNDER-VOLTAGE POWER OFF and powers off; >4.4V reports OVER-VOLTAGE POWER OFF and powers off.

power.method/procedure: Table 38 states VBAT=4.0V and says its values are typical module values tested in laboratory.

environmental.method/procedure: Table 39 gives contact- and air-discharge results at temperature 25℃ and humidity 45%.
The module constantly monitors its temperature.
environmental.explicit_pass_fail_criteria: ≥+80℃ reports +CMTE: 1; ≤-30℃ reports +CMTE:-1; >+85℃ reports +CMTE: 2 and powers off; <-40℃ reports +CMTE:-2 and powers off.

ambiguities.issue: The GPRS class statements differ within this same edition: page 10 says “class 12/class 10 (optional),” while page 11 says “class 12 (default)” and “class 1~12 (option).” Both are retained rather than reconciled.

Sleep/current labels are not fully aligned: page 11 calls 0.65 mA “sleep mode” with AT+CFUN=0, page 25 labels <fun>=0 minimum functionality and reports 0.65 mA, and page 49 labels sleep current with AT+CFUN=1. Values and labels are reported verbatim.
The pin table names pin 68 GPS_ANT, while the GNSS antenna narrative calls the interface GNSS_ANT. The JSON preserves the pin-table label and the narrative separately.
Section numbering around GNSS/antenna is inconsistent: the contents labels GNSS as 4.15 and antenna as 4.16, but the body uses “4.16.1 GNSS Overview” and then “4.16. Antenna Interface.”
Physical page 45 says the active-antenna arrangement is “shown in Figure 54,” although the supplied figure index names GNSS active antenna matching circuit as Figure 40; no correction is inferred.
Several figures are diagram-based and text extraction does not preserve full spatial wiring. Circuit descriptions in this JSON are limited to readable labels and surrounding prose.
